nodes.text: Let $(A_i)$ be a family of countably infinite sets such that $\lvert A_i\cap A_j\rvert \neq 2$ for all $i\neq j$. Find the smallest cardinal $C$ such that $\cup A_i$ can always be coloured with at most $C$ colours so that no $A_i$ is monochromatic.

#603 : [Er87] combinatorics | set theory A problem of Komjáth. If instead we have $\lvert A_i\cap A_jvert 
eq 1$ then Komjáth showed that this is possible with at most $\aleph_0$ colours. GPT 5.4 Pro (prompted by Chojecki) proved there is no uniform bound on such $C$: for every cardinal $C$ there is a family of countably infinite sets $(A_i)$ such that $\lvert A_i\cap A_jvert 
eq 2$ for all $i
eq j$, and in any colouring of $\cup A_i$ with $C$ colours some $A_i$ is monochromatic. Indeed, by the Erdős-Rado theorem , if $\kappa$ is the successor of $2^C$, any $C$-colouring of the edges of the complete graph on $\kappa$ vertices contains a monochromatic countably infinite complete graph, and hence we can take $(A_i)$ to be the collection of all countably infinite complete graphs (since any two such intersect in either countably infinite or $ inom{n}{2}$ many edges for some finite $n$, and in particular never intersect exactly twice).
